output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initialSupply and mintedAmount are added without checking if the result would overflow the balanceOf the target address, allowing the owner to set the balance of any user to any value, if a user interacts with a minted contract.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The function adds _value to balanceOf[msg.sender] without checking if the result would overflow the sender's balance, allowing users to cause a denial of service (balance becomes frozen).

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The function adds _value to balanceOf[_to] without checking if the result would overflow the recipient's balance, allowing users to cause a denial of service (balance becomes frozen).

The approve function has a wrong logic vulnerability. The function does not check if _value is zero before setting allowance to zero, allowing users to approve a spender to spend their funds, if they mistakenly call approve with a value of 0.

The receiveApproval function has a bad randomness function. The function uses a simple mapping to check if an address is a spender, allowing attackers to predict the spender addresses, if an attacker can control the target addresses.
